flashcard_questions.q: What is a nebula in the life cycle of a star?
flashcard_questions.a: A vast cloud of hydrogen gas and dust from which stars are born.

flashcard_questions.q: At roughly what core temperature does hydrogen begin to fuse into helium in a protostar?
What name is given to the balance between outward fusion pressure and inward gravity in a star?
Life cycle of a Sun-sized star: main sequence → ____ → planetary nebula → ____
Life cycle of a massive star: main sequence → ____ → supernova → neutron star or black hole
Which remnant forms when the core left after a supernova is between about 1.4 and 3 solar masses?
Which remnant forms when the core left after a supernova is above about 3 solar masses?
Which elements can only be created during a supernova?
What does red-shift tell you about a distant galaxy?
flashcard_questions.a: It is moving away from us, so its light waves are stretched to longer wavelengths.

flashcard_questions.q: What did Edwin Hubble discover about a galaxy's distance and its red-shift?
flashcard_questions.a: The further away a galaxy is, the greater its red-shift.

flashcard_questions.q: What is cosmic microwave background radiation?
flashcard_questions.a: Leftover thermal radiation from the Big Bang, now cooled to about 2.7 K.

flashcard_questions.q: How long ago did the universe begin according to the Big Bang theory?
What proportion of the universe is thought to be dark matter?
What proportion of the universe is thought to be dark energy?
How long does a satellite in geostationary orbit take to complete one revolution?

notes: 15 cards: 3 term→definition (nebula, CMBR, hydrostatic equilibrium), 2 process-order cloze cards for the two stellar life cycles, 6 value cards taken verbatim (15 million °C, 1.4–3 and >3 solar masses, 13.8 billion years, 27%, 68%, 24 hours), 2 evidence cards (red-shift, Hubble), 1 supernova-element card. Dropped the planet order, the balloon analogy and the dark-matter rotation evidence to stay inside 15; the lesson is broad, so I prioritised the named values and life-cycle sequences.
